title: Full recitation with tartil: Al-Muddaththir: rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 1: Al-Muddaththir and madd in recitation
source: Written for quran/y9 lesson 23 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Full recitation with tartil rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 23. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

head: Madd
When
Counts (Hafs)
Example
rows: Madd letter, nothing after it causes more
Hamza after the madd letter, same word
Stopping on the letter after a madd letter

keywords.def: lengthening a vowel sound, counted in beats (harakat)

questions.q: Recite 74:1 to 10 at tartil pace and name each madd you stretched.
questions.a: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا munfasil; ثِيَابَكَ tabi'i; ٱلنَّاقُورِ 'arid at a stop; يَسِيرٍ 'arid at a stop.

questions.q: Breakout pairs: recite the whole surah between you (alternate scenes) at tartil pace; partner scores fluency and madd (pupil PDF). Today's rota group recites to the teacher.
questions.a: Partner scores; teacher records rota scores.

questions.q: Extend: write your 'arid length choice and why.
questions.a: e.g. 4 counts: steady and easy to keep consistent.

questions.q: Stretch: recite the whole surah alone at tartil pace.

options: Steady pace, even madd, stops at ayah ends
questions.a: A) Steady pace, even madd, stops at ayah ends. Tartil is measured and clear.

questions.q: Think again: Tartil is not fast and not slow. How would you describe it to a younger pupil?
questions.a: Clear and steady, giving every letter and rule its right, so the listener can follow.
